publicTransport.label: Public Transport Accessibility
publicTransport.description:
Guidelines for assessing public transport accessibility
Urban: Very Poor = hardly any practical public transport, very low frequency, key destinations difficult to reach, high car dependency.
Urban: Poor = limited usability and flexibility; key destinations require significant travel time.
Urban: Average = adequate for basic daily needs, regular services, key destinations accessible.
Urban: Good = practical daily connectivity, regular and reliable services, good access to key amenities.
Urban: Very Good = above-average mobility without a car, fast links to key hubs, high day-to-day flexibility.
Urban: Excellent = outstanding mobility, almost all daily needs accessible without a car, excellent access to key destinations.
Rural: Very Poor = virtually no practical public transport, high car dependency, key amenities difficult to reach.
Rural: Poor = limited day-to-day usability and flexibility; key destinations require significant travel time.
Rural: Average = adequate for basic daily needs, regular services available, regional amenities accessible.
Rural: Good = good regional public transport, regular and reliable services, good access to surrounding centres.
Rural: Very Good = above-average public transport for a rural location, practical for daily life without a car.
Rural: Excellent = exceptional mobility for a rural region, almost all daily needs accessible without a car.

scores.1: Very Poor
scores.6: Excellent

individualTransport.label: Private Transport Accessibility
individualTransport.description:
Guidelines for assessing private transport accessibility
Very Poor: severely restricted access, remote location, long journeys to regional centres, poor links to principal roads.
Poor: below-average road access, limited regional accessibility, longer journeys to key destinations.
Average: average accessibility, regional centres generally reachable, acceptable traffic conditions.
Good: good regional accessibility, principal roads easily accessible, practical for daily use.
Very Good: very good regional and national accessibility, fast links to key centres, highly attractive for commuters.
Excellent: outstanding regional and national road links, excellent access to key destinations, exceptionally high mobility quality.

scores.1: Very Poor
scores.6: Excellent

infrastructure.label: Neighbourhood Amenities
infrastructure.description:
Guidelines for assessing neighbourhood amenities
Very Poor: virtually no local amenities nearby.
Poor: only limited basic amenities.
Average: supermarket and basic amenities available.
Good: supermarket, doctors and schools within 10–15 minutes.
Very Good: several shops, doctors and restaurants.
Excellent: almost all amenities within walking distance.

scores.1: Very Poor
scores.6: Excellent

scores.6: premium environment with exceptionally high residential quality

scores.2: beside a busy road, motorway junction, commercial or industrial area
scores.3: beside an urban main road, bus route or tram line
scores.4: quiet side street near a principal road
scores.5: quiet residential area, far from main roads, with green spaces nearby
scores.6: suburban or rural location with extensive green space and fields

scores.3: Older but functional system; modernisation advisable in due course.
scores.4: Sound and well-maintained condition; no immediate investment requirement evident.
scores.5: Modern and efficient heating system; low likelihood of medium-term investment.
scores.6: As-new or comprehensively modernised heating system; low long-term investment requirement expected.
